layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The general viewpoint is that local breakdown of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive state, usually observed in pitting corrosion, is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: primarily due to the presence of halogen ions in the ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ternal passivating medium.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been proved time and again by direct experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments that the breakdown of passivity is preceded by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the adsorption of halogen ions on the metal surface.1, 5, 7

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This, however, does not explain the well-defined local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nature of pitting corrosion. The theories advanced on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion offer different explanations for the lo-

layout_dets.text: cal nature of this type of corrosion, namely: penetration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the double layer, due to fluctuations in the thermal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: tribute the process of pitting developments to the estab-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lishment of more or less stable anodic areas on the pas-

layout_dets.text: sive metal surface.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Of particular practical importance are the investiga-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions on the pitting corrosion phenomenon of stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels, inasmuch as this type of corrosion destruction defi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: material in modern technology.

layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This investigation was conducted because the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development of new alloys with increased re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistance to pitting corrosion appears to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: largely dependent on an understanding of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects of various concentrations of alloying ele-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments on the initiation and steady operation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized pitting sites on the metal surface.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Corrosion tests in 0.5N FeCl3 and determi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nations of passivity breakdown potentials in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.1N NaCl were employed to study the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tendencies of 18 Cr-14Ni stainless steels to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which alloying elements in various concentra-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions had been added. The alloying elements,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chosen for their stability in solutions containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride ions and their solubility in austenite,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were: Mo, Si, V, W, Ti, Ce, Nb, Ta, Zr and Re.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, Si and V, respectively, at 5 percent con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: centration, had the most marked effect in in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creasing resistance to pitting. Re, even in con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: centrations below 1 percent, was also very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effective. The other elements tested had either

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a negative influence or no effect.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Heat treatment in the dangerous tempera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture zone (650 C for 2 hours) greatly impaired

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the resistance of steel alloyed with 5 percent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, Si or V, which is not susceptible to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion in the quenched state.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Although, as pointed out above, there may be a num-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ber of reasons for the breach in passivity of separate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: local points on the stainless steel surface, the primary,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: basic reason must be the possible, if not practically the in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variable, existence of heterogeneity in the metal struc

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture and composition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus, according to the data in Reference 9, pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occurs mainly at the grain boundaries. It is a well known

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fact that, as far as physical structure and chemical com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position are concerned, the grain boundaries differ from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the bulk of the grain and precipitation of secondary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phases and accumulation of impurities are liable to oc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cur at the grain boundaries. For this reason the passive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state at the grain boundaries is lower in proctetive prop-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erties than on the grain proper. It seems that the site

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where pitting develops also depends on the character of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the surface pretreatment and on the aggressiveness of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the electrolyte.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In some instances, pitting may be due to the precipi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation of secondary phases resulting in heterogeneity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal composition. In the presence of ferritic inclusions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic steels become increasingly susceptible to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion. This may be due to the fact that at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundaries with the ferritic inclusions, austenitic areas

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are depleted in chromium, because of the increase in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium content of the ferrite.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The compositions of stainless steels along with their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures play a decisive role as far as pitting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is concerned. A most positive effect on the resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels to pitting corrosion can be observed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloying these steels with elements capable of increasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the stability of their passive state, such as chromium,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and molybdenum.9,13 An increase in the nickel and ni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trogen contents of chromium-nickel steels also increases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their resistance to pitting corrosion. The positive effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown by these elements is believed to be due to the for-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation of a more stable, homogeneous austenitic struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture.9 According to Reference 9, alloying with small con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: centrations of silicon (up to 2.5 percent) increases the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of the alloy to pitting corrosion, due to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changes produced at the grain boundaries. According to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other data,14 the positive effect produced by silicon is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to the increased stability of the passive state, re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sulting from the increase in the silicon content of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protective film.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There still remains a broad field for research on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem of fighting corrosion of stainless steels by spe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cial alloying. First of all, the effect of various alloying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements on the variations in the intensity and the na-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture of pitting corrosion has not as yet been adequately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studied. Secondly, there is still no clear concept about

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the mechanisms involved in rendering stainless steels less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: susceptible to pitting corrosion by the specific effect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloying elements. To date, there is still no clean-cut

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: answer to the question of whether the main and primary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1—Effect of alloying elements on the rate of corrosion of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 18Cr-14Ni steel in 0.5N FeCl3. The test lasted 68 hours at room

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect of alloying elements is to reduce the probability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the development of pits in initial corrosion sites, or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whether the effect is purely that of retardation of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rate of development of these pitting sites. Solution of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these problems is naturally of great importance to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development of new alloys endowed with increased re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistance to pitting corrosion.

layout_dets.text: Experimental Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This work, therefore, is primarily devoted to the ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects produced by different alloying elements in increas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the resistance of austenitic chromium-nickel steels to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion and to site initiation and spread of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion, depending on the steel composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The first experimental alloys were based on CRES steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the type 18Cr-14Ni, which had the following per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: centage composition: Cr,17.93; Ni,14.38; C,0.036; addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional alloying elements: Mo, Si, V, W, Ti, Ce, Nb, Ta,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zr, Re, i.e., elements possessing some degree of stability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in solutions containing Cl ions and endowed with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marked solubility in austenite. Each of these supplemen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tal alloying elements was introduced in the following

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentrations: Mo, W, Si, V,1, 2 and 5, respectively;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spectively; Re, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2.5 percent. The content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of these alloying elements in the alloys, according to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chemical analysis data, is presented in Table 1. Con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sidering that Mo, W and V are ferrite-forming elements,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the aforementioned steel, with increased Ni content, was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taken to preserve the austenitic structure. Thirty differ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent compositions were thus prepared and investigated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The steels were smelted in an electric induction fur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nace under slag. The ingots were forged, rolled into bars

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 mm thick, then tempered at 1150 C (heating for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 15 minutes) and quenched in water. Metallographic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: examination after quenching showed that the steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: had an austenitic structure and that only the steel with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 percent Si exhibited an α phase.

layout_dets.text: Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pitting Corrosion Resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It follows from the data obtained that the alloys most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistant to pitting corrosion are the steels alloyed with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 percent Mo, 5 percent V and 5 percent Si. The cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion rate of these steel specimens was of the order of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: magnitude 0.01 gm/sq m/hour, with external appearance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unchanged and the same as before experimental ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posures. Considerable increase in resistance to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion is also exhibited by steels alloyed with 2.5

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: percent V, 2.5 percent Si, 2.5 percent Mo and 0.2-1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: percent Re. It must be pointed out that unlike other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metals, Re produces a considerable effect in enhancing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the resistance of steels to pitting corrosion at much lower

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentrations of the element in the alloy, compared to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, V and Si. A number of alloying elements such as Ti,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ce or Nb, have a negative effect. For Ta and W com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pletely indeterminate results were obtained. Apparently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these elements affect the susceptibility of the steel to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion but little.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: percent V and 0.2-1 percent Re are most resistant to

layout_dets.text: experiments. The considerable reduction in the suscepti-

layout_dets.text: with vanadium and rhenium was first established in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Si and V. These experiments were performed both in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Summary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Investigations were conducted on the effect of sup-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plementary alloying of 18Cr-14Ni stainless steels with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, Si, V, Re, W, Ti, Ce, Nb,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Ta with respect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to susceptibility to pitting corrosion. Corrosion tests in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.5N FeCl3 and determinations of the breakdown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials in 0.1N NaCl solutions were employed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. It was demonstrated that the most positive effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is exerted by Mo, Si and V. At a concentration of 5

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: percent in 18Cr-14Ni steels, these elements impart high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance to pitting corrosion. Alloying with Re, even

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in small concentrations (up to 1 percent) is highly ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fective in increasing the resistance of the steel to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion. Ti, Nb and Ce have a negative effect on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance to pitting corrosion; Zr, Ta and W have no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. In 18Cr-14Ni steels, pitting initiates in the periph-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eral regions of the grains. On alloying this steel with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, V or Si, pitting most probably initiates directly at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the grain boundaries.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Enhanced pitting corrosion resistance exhibited by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels alloyed with 5 percent Mo, 5 percent Si, 5 per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cent V or 2.5 percent Re can be explained by the greater

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: :tability of the passive state, due to the higher corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of the passive film, resulting from the inclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of these alloying elements in the composition of the pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tective film.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Heat treatment in the dangerous temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zone (650 C for 2 hours) of steel not susceptible to pit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting corrosion in the quenched state (alloyed with 5 per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Si or V) strongly impairs the resistance of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel to pitting corrosion when alloyed with Si and V.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Steels alloyed with Mo or Re become susceptible to inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: granular corrosion after annealing.

layout_dets.text: DISCUSSIONS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Question by J. Kruger, National Bureau of Standards,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Washington, D.C.:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Did the heterogeneity you mentioned as the effect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the addition elements refer to the effect of the hetero-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: geneity of the metal on the properties of the oxide film?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reply by N. D. Tomashov:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The heterogeneity of the 18 Cr-14 Ni stainless steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was not decreased by the additional alloying with Mo,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Si, V or Re. We suppose that the increase in resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion of these alloys is a result of improving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the passive film corrosion resistance due to presence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloying elements in the protective film composition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion curves of stainless steel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The influence of additional alloying components such

layout_dets.text: as Mo, Si, V and Re on the secondary passivity range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 18 Cr-14 Ni stainless steel was not examined in this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study.

layout_dets.text: Have you also exposed these stainless steels to sea

layout_dets.text: Reply by N. D. Tomashov:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We did not carry out such tests with these stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the test the most resistant-to-pitting corrosion steels in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sea water, too.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, Chicago, Ill.:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Have you studied the effect of two alloying compo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nents simultaneously? Could it occur that pitting inhibi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion by, for instance, 5.0 percent Mo and 2.0 percent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Re, is much larger than simply additive? Is there any

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indication of such synergistic effects?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reply by N. D. Tomashov:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The eventual effect of two alloying components simul-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taneously introduced was not investigated in this work.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There are reasons to expect that such an influence may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be larger or more effective than that of a singular added

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloying component. We intend to confirm it experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentally in our subsequent work.
